videos.desc: In this video I will show how to  create a program in Spike prime classroom that allows you to turn a robot to a given angle using the built in gyro sensor, and a proportional controller.

5 bar linkage made from coreless servo motors, AS5600 encoders, BTS7960 motor drivers, a teensy 4.1, and 3D printed parts. This is a test leg setup for my future quadrupedal robot project. Contact me at printedgadgets@gmail.com if you want more information.

Third robot dog. 
 
- 12 DOF 
- 12 x 20kg servos (only $150 altogether) 
- more dynamic than v1 or v2
- walks like a newborn deer

This is my second attempt at a robot dog. 

- 8 DOF 
- light weight 
- 8 x 35kg servos 
- no controller

This is a 12 DOF 3D printed quadrupedal robot that I designed. It uses 12 servo motors, a Polulu maestro servo controller, and a Teensy 4.1 microcontroller.  For more information, check out my instructable.

https://www.instructables.com/3D-Printed-Robot-Dog/

videos.t: I Built a Robot Dog and Made it Dance
videos.desc:
In this video, I'll be building TOPS ,  my robot dog. While I have attempted a couple of robot dogs in the past, nothing has come close to having the natural gait of an actual dog. In this project, the goal is to make a more dynamic quadrupedal robot. Be sure to watch parts 0, 1, and 2 for context. Subscribe if you enjoyed the video!
